forces.title: GenAI drives personalized targeting and creative content for ads
forces.description: Generative AI is gaining traction for personalized targeting, 1:1 marketing, and content creation such as ad copywriting, social media engagement, and real-time consumer content. This enables advertisers to create more relevant and engaging campaigns at scale. For Digital Advertising & Ad Tech, this represents a significant tailwind by enhancing the capabilities of programmatic platforms, DSPs, and attribution analytics to deliver hyper-personalized experiences.
forces.source_title: Southeast Asia: What's Happening with Consumers and Consumer Products

forces.title: Shift from SEO to Generative Search Optimization (GEO)
forces.description: The rise of GenAI platforms as search engines is fundamentally changing how consumers discover information, moving from 'Google it' to 'ask ChatGPT'. Brands will need to ensure their content and products are surfaced prominently and accurately through 'generative engine optimization' (GEO). This is a structural change for ad tech, requiring platforms to adapt to AI-driven search environments and develop new optimization strategies to maintain visibility and advertiser ROI.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Technology, Media and Telecoms (TMT) H1 2025 Insights / H2 2025 Outlook September 2025

forces.title: Agentic AI enables autonomous ad campaign optimization
forces.description: Agentic AI, which can act autonomously, assess situations, make plans, and execute tasks with minimal human intervention, is emerging. This technology allows for the optimization, automation, and execution of routine tasks in advertising based on logic and adaptation through experience. For ad tech, this signifies a structural shift towards more autonomous campaign management, potentially increasing efficiency and reducing operational costs for advertisers using programmatic platforms.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Technology, Media and Telecoms (TMT) H1 2025 Insights / H2 2025 Outlook September 2025

forces.title: Challenges in AI deployment, explainability, and ethical governance
forces.description: Despite widespread interest, businesses face significant challenges in deploying AI at scale, including issues with reproducibility, explainability, data quality, and ethical governance. The risk of AI systems amplifying biases or making opaque decisions without proper oversight is high. For ad tech, these challenges present a key risk, as the effectiveness and trustworthiness of AI-driven platforms depend heavily on robust governance, transparent operations, and reliable data inputs.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Technology, Media and Telecoms (TMT) H1 2025 Insights / H2 2025 Outlook September 2025

forces.title: Diversified digital content sources require multichannel ad strategies
forces.description: Consumers are influenced by a diverse blend of digital content sources for inspiration, including social media (Instagram, TikTok, YouTube), search engines, online travel agencies (OTAs), and brand websites. This necessitates advertisers to adopt multichannel strategies reaching beyond single platforms. For ad tech, this is a tailwind, driving demand for platforms that can manage and optimize campaigns across various digital channels and provide integrated attribution analytics.

forces.title: Precision influencer marketing emerges as key digital advertising channel
forces.description: Influencer marketing is a powerful force, with precision campaigns demonstrating significantly higher efficiency and sales impact. Influencers are the top channel for new brand/product exploration, particularly in emotionally-driven sectors. This structural shift highlights the growing demand for ad tech solutions that can identify target consumer 'tribes,' manage influencer relationships, and provide analytics for optimizing these highly effective digital campaigns.

forces.title: Increased internet penetration expands digital advertising reach
forces.description: Overall internet penetration continues to increase, providing a larger audience base for digital advertising. This trend is a fundamental tailwind for the Digital Advertising & Ad Tech sector. A growing online population directly expands the addressable market for programmatic platforms, DSPs, and other ad tech solutions, driving higher demand and potential revenue growth for companies connecting advertisers to these audiences.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Technology, Media and Telecoms (TMT) H1 2025 Insights / H2 2025 Outlook September 2025

forces.title: Advanced data and social technology critical for influencer marketing
forces.description: Winning in precision influencer marketing requires robust capabilities in data and social technology, including global access to social tech tools, on-demand analytics, and tooling support. The hyperfocused use of consumer data (social listening, demographics, behavioral insights) is key. This is a significant tailwind for ad tech firms specializing in data analytics, audience segmentation, and platform integration, enabling more effective and measurable influencer campaigns.

forces.title: Decline in Venture Capital funding for Irish SMEs
forces.description: Venture capital funding for Irish SMEs fell to its lowest level in ten years in Q2 2025, with a substantial decline in investment attributed to retracting international investors. This reduction in capital flows poses a headwind for indigenous startups, including those in the ad tech sector. Decreased funding can hinder innovation, slow growth, and limit the ability of smaller ad tech companies to compete or scale their platforms.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Technology, Media and Telecoms (TMT) H1 2025 Insights / H2 2025 Outlook September 2025

viewpoints.title: Online consumption drives demand for digital-first media models
viewpoints.description: In H1 2025, online consumption became the dominant source of news in Ireland, surpassing traditional media like radio, TV, and newspapers. This shift reinforces the critical need for media businesses to adopt digital-first models. The changing media landscape creates significant opportunities for digital advertising and ad tech platforms that facilitate online content monetization and audience engagement.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Technology, Media and Telecoms (TMT) H1 2025 Insights / H2 2025 Outlook September 2025

viewpoints.title: Internet advertising poised for rapid expansion with AI and personalization
viewpoints.description: Internet advertising revenue in Ireland is projected for rapid expansion, driven by increasing internet penetration and AI-enabled hyper-personalization and targeted advertising. Digital video advertising (DVA) is identified as the fastest-growing category. This indicates a strong tailwind for digital advertising and ad tech companies that can leverage advanced AI capabilities to deliver more effective and personalized campaigns.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Technology, Media and Telecoms (TMT) H1 2025 Insights / H2 2025 Outlook September 2025

viewpoints.title: Irish Entertainment & Media sector forecasted for steady growth through 2029
viewpoints.description: Ireland's Entertainment and Media sector is projected to achieve an annual growth rate of 3.3% through 2029. While physical media declines, the overall sector benefits from digital transformation, with internet advertising being a key growth driver. This provides a supportive environment for pure-play ad tech companies operating within the digital media ecosystem, as their services are integral to monetizing online content.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Technology, Media and Telecoms (TMT) H1 2025 Insights / H2 2025 Outlook September 2025

viewpoints.title: Precision influencer marketing significantly boosts campaign efficiency and sales
viewpoints.description: Precision influencer marketing is proving highly effective, with well-executed campaigns being six times more efficient at reaching target shoppers and boosting sales by up to 20% in the first month compared to traditional influencer efforts. This approach relies on deep consumer understanding and data-driven insights. This highlights the growing importance of sophisticated ad tech platforms that enable precise targeting, analytics, and measurement for influencer campaigns.

viewpoints.title: Cautious business approach to AI adoption despite widespread interest
viewpoints.description: Despite significant hype and 98% of businesses having started their AI journey, only 6% have deployed the technology at scale, with many relying on third-party off-the-shelf solutions. Issues like reproducibility, explainability, data quality, and ethical governance remain challenges. This cautious approach could slow the full integration of advanced AI capabilities into ad tech platforms, limiting immediate transformative impact despite its long-term potential.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Technology, Media and Telecoms (TMT) H1 2025 Insights / H2 2025 Outlook September 2025

demand_drivers.description: A broader user base online directly translates to more opportunities for digital advertising reach and engagement, fueling revenue growth.
The ability to deliver highly targeted and relevant ads through AI increases advertising effectiveness and ROI for brands, driving higher spend in the sector.

market_sizing.methodology: Revenue from internet advertising in Ireland, forecasted based on PwC's Entertainment & Media Outlook report.
market_sizing.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Technology, Media and Telecoms (TMT) H1 2025 Insights / H2 2025 Outlook September 2025

demand_drivers.description: More users online and greater access to high-speed internet support the consumption and delivery of video content, expanding the audience for DVA.
AI allows for more relevant and engaging video ad placements, improving campaign performance and encouraging increased advertiser investment in DVA.
The majority of DVA spending will come from mobile by 2030, indicating a strong consumer preference for video content on mobile devices, which drives DVA growth.
